_removed_note: drop-bytecode-isolation and drop-mtime-bump both SURVIVE individually because the two invalidation guards (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE env var + os.utime mtime bump) are jointly sufficient and individually redundant. Removing either alone leaves the other covering, so neither single-anchor mutant can kill. Both-at-once is not expressible under the single-anchor-per-mutant schema. Pending the expect:survived control-mutant feature.

mutants.name: score-any-nonzero-as-killed
mutants.why: the scoring arm's core claim — only exit 1 is KILLED. If this survives, any non-zero exit (timeouts, collection errors) could be miscounted as kills.

mutants.name: drop-baseline-control
mutants.why: the green-baseline positive control — a red baseline means the test was already failing, so a 'kill' is meaningless. If this survives, the suite does not actually require the baseline gate.
